senses.gloss: to swing, lift up; trnsf. to hold in high esteem.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 7:2:5">Y. Ber. VII, 11ᵇ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 5:3:4">Y. Naz. V, end, 54ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 91">Gen. R. s. 91</cite>, a. e. it is written in the Book of Ben Sira <he>סַלְסְלֶיהָ ותרוממך ובין וכ׳</he> hold her (the Torah) high, and she will uplift thee and seat thee between princes (v.
Pesik. R. s. 20 להרכיבה … ולסַלְסְלָהּ בכל וכ׳ to let her ride on an elephant … and raise her among all the nobles of the kingdom; a. e.—Part. pass. מְסוּלְסָל (v. סֹלֶת) select, sublime.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:1">Cant. R. to I, 1</cite> <he>המעולה שבשירים המס׳ שבשירים</he> the loftiest, the sublimest of songs.

senses.gloss: (cmp. שלשל) to turn, to plait, esp. to curl the hair.
units: Pesik. R. s. 26 הרי מְסַלְסֵל קווצותיו behold, he (Elijah) curls his locks! Meg. 18ᵃ; R. Hash. 26ᵇ (ref. to Prov. IV, 8) the Rabbis did not know what sals’leha meant, until they heard Rabbi’s handmaid say to one twirling his hair, עד מתי אתה מסלסל בשערך how long wilt thou curl thy hair (from which they deduced that sals’leha meant, ‘turn the law in all directions’); Naz. 3ᵃ.

<cite ref="Mishnah Nazir 1:1">Ib. I, 1</cite> if one vowing uses the expression <he>הריני מסלסֹל וכ׳</he> ‘I will be a hair-curler’, he is a Nazarite; Y. ib. I, 51ᵇ top <he>כאומר הריני מן המְסַלְסְלִין</he> it is as if saying, I will be one of those wearing curled locks. Ib. <he>אֲסַלְסֵל</he> I will curl my hair.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 80:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. LXXX</cite> (expl. <cite ref="Q02127"><he>פתואל</he></cite>) <he>שהיה מסלסל בשערו וכ׳</he> he curled his hair like a maiden (v. <cite ref="Q02182"><he>פָּתַל</he></cite>); a. e.—[

senses.gloss: to commit lewdness, v. סָלַל I.]—[Yalk. Kings 232 מסלסלת, v. צִלְצֵל.]
